lecture_14.title: CS336 Spring 2026, Lecture 14: Data II (transformation, filtering, deduplication, mixing, post-training data)
lecture_14.note: Line anchors refer to the local shallow clone (sha256 8e0e17f8..., recorded in discovered.json). Nothing in this file runs on a GPU. Of the 16 @inspect values, those that are plain arithmetic (jaccard L230, prob_collision L298, the three probs dicts L303/L306/L309, threshold L316, prob_match L319, prob_collision L321, low/high_num_epochs L363-L364, ratio L397, downsampled_source_token_counts L398) are re-evaluated by this thread and stated as 'evaluating the professor's formula gives'. Three @inspect values depend on the mmh3 library, which is not installed here: h = mmh3.hash('hello') (L188) is NOT restated; deduped_items (L204) is stated only as 'five strings, one of the two identical hello removed, in hash order'; estimated_jaccard (L262) is stated only as 'within 0.01 of 0.6', which is what the assert at L263 guarantees. The keep_document rule (L109-L110) is code without @inspect; this thread derives its keep probability from numpy's Pareto definition and marks that derivation as inference. Every number the professor reads off a cited paper (OpenMathText thresholds and 14.7B tokens, phi-1 HumanEval 12.19%/17.68%, C4 61,036 repeats, Lee et al. n = 9000 / b = 20 / r = 450, OpenThoughts 1.2M / 27 sources / 16 responses, SWE-smith 128 repos / 50K tasks, SWE-Zero 300K / 150K / 13K, SWE-rebench 21K / 3.4K / 450K, SWE-ZERO-12M 12M / 32K / 120K / 50.4 pass@100) is quoted with that attribution and never asserted as this thread's own. Numbers that live only inside embedded figures (dclm-wet.png, data-filtering-scale.png, regmix.png, data-mixing-methods.png, the two LSH S-curve images, the OpenThoughts/SWE result images) are recorded as shown and not restated.
